full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J. :-This appeal by leave granted on 8.11.1995 is for consideration of the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant namely, first, that the area of the C.S. Khatian No. 191 was 5.74 which has been recorded in the two R.S. Khatian No. 690 with an area of 4.50 acres and R.S. Khatian No. 691 with an area of 1.24 acres and the contesting defendant Respondent No. 1 claimed only 1.24 acres of R.S. Khatian No. 691 which is the part and parcel of the C.S. Khatian No. 191 and this was never denied by the defendant-respondent either in the lower court or in the lower appellate court and, as such, the question of identity and repayment does not arise at the revisional stage, secondly, that the lower appellate Court after considering the evidence both oral and documentary found possession of the plaintiff in the suit land but the High Court Division on misappreciation of the evidence on record most illegally held that the lower appellate court's finding of possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land was contrary to material evidence on record and this finding of the High Court Division is wit:,--L airy iiasi3 whatsoever and lastly, that both the trial court and the lower appellate court, found possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and this finding of fact ought not to have been altered by the High Court Division in the revisional jurisdiction. 

2. Plaintiff-appellants filed a suit for declaration of title stating, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 191 measuring 5.74 decimals was acquired by Tajumuddin Matbar on the basis of registered Patta dated 7th Aswin, 1281 B.S.: that Tajumuddin Matbar died before C.S. operation leaving one son Panjat All and one daughter Pearjan and after the death of his father Panjat Ali being a minor lived with his sister Pearjan who was married in the house of Nizamuddin. father-in-law of Pearjan and accordingly Nizamuddin became the de-facto guardian of Panjat Ali and, thus the property acquired by Tajumuddin Matbar on the basis of Patta dated 7th Aswin, 1281 B.S. was under the management and control of Nizamuddin and during the time of C.S. record aforesaid Patta land in C.S. Khatian No.191 was recorded in the names, Nizamuddin 1/3rd share. Ahmed (brother of Nizamuddin) 1/3rd share and Panjat Ali 1/3rd share although the property ought to have been recorded in 2/3rd share in the name of Panjat Ali and in 1/3rd share in the name of Pearjan; that immediately after the C.S. record Panjat Ali died leaving his sister Pearjan as his sole heir and accordingly Pearjan became the sole owner of the entire property left by Tajumuddin Matbar and thereafter Pearjan died leaving behind one son Hakimuddin who also was killed and survived by his two sons namely, Nurul Huq and Shamsul Huq, present plaintiff-appellants, and one daughter Noor Meher and a widow Rupjan and during the life time of Noor Meher and Rupjan they gifted their share to the plaintiff and thus the plain-tiffs became the sole owners of the property recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 191; that it has been further stated in the plaint that during R.S. operation the plaintiffs were minor and the land of C.S. Khatian No. 191 was also wrongly recorded in R.S. Khatian Nos. 690 and 691 which was subsequently recorded in S.A. Khatian Nos. 836 and 311 and though the entire land ought to have been recorded in the names of the plaintiffs but only 2 annas 15 gondas share of R.S. Khatian No. 690 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 830 has been recorded in the name of the plaintiff and the other recorded persons have or had no title and possession in any portion of the lands in R.S. as well as in S.A. Khatian of the suit land. 

3. Defendant No. 6, Lutfor Rahman contested the suit claiming only 1.24 acres of S.A. Khatian No. 311 on the allegation that the R.S. recorded tenant Rahimjan made kolraiyati pattan of 1.24 acres of land to Kaisar Ahmed who is the recorded tenant of S.A. Khatian No. 311 and subsequently Kaisar Ahmed sold the land to Defendant No. 6. None of the defendants except Defendant No. 6 denied the title and possession of the plaintiffs. The further contention of Defendant No. 6 is that Tajumuddin had 1/3rd share in the suit property who died leaving a son Panjat Ali and daughter Pearjan; that Panjat Ali died leaving a sister Pearjan as his sole heir, Nizamuddin and Ahmed All had 2/3rd shares in the Khatian as per C.S. Khatian; that Nizamuddin died leaving two sons Aptar Ali and Amzad Ali and Amzad All died leaving behind three sons, three daughters and a wife, Ahmed Ali Heba gifted the entire share to Panjat Ali; that Pearjan and the heirs of Amjad Ali settled 1.23 acres of land with one Rahimjan in 1316 B.S. at a jama of Tk. 16/- and Rahimjan had been in possession of the suit land since her pattan. Rahimjan again settled 1.40 acres of land to Kaisar Ahmed by registered patta dated 10th Baisakh, 1352 B.S. and 1.24 acres of land stood recorded in the name of Kaisar Ahmed correctly that while in possession in that land Kaisar Ahmed sold his land to Defendant No. 6 by a kabala dated 27th Aswin, 1374 B.S. and Defendant No. 6 have been possessing the same since then. The plaintiffs filed a Partition suit being T.S. No. 184 of 1960 which was dis-missed; that thereafter another T.S. No. 207 of 1979 was filed which was also dis-missed. The present suit has also been brought on some false allegations and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. The suit was dismissed and on appeal the same was, reversed decreeing the suit. The Defendant No. 6 moved the High Court Division Civil Revision No. 3239 of 1991 and the Rule was made absolute setting aside the judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge restoring the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the impugned judgment and order. The plaintiff thereafter moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid leave to appeal. 

5. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant has taken us though the judgments of the Courts below, the plaint and the relevant papers on record and submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in making out a third case that the suit land can-not be definitely ascertained without relayment with the land of patta dated 17th Aswin, 1281 B.S. in order to see as to whether the land was identical or not inasmuch as in view of the rent receipt Ext. E series lead to a presumption of possession in favour of the defendant the findings of the lower appellate Court regarding possession of the plaintiff was contrary to the evidence on record. The learned Advocate further submits that the finding as to the possession of the final Court of fact has been disturbed by the High Court Division on misappreciation of the evidence on record inasmuch as the D. Ws. have themselves supported the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and as such the finding of the High Court Division is not only contrary to the material evidence on record but without any basis whatsoever. 

6. Mr. Menhazuddin Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents has however relying on Ext. B the certified copy of patta dated 10th Baisak 1352 B.S. and Ext. C kabala dated 27th Aswin 1374 B.S. has sought to argue that Rahimjan, the predecessor of Kaisar Ahmed has obtained the settlement of 1.23 acres of land on 23.4.1945 at a jama of Tk. 16/- and having possessed settled 1.40 acres in favour of Kaiser which has been correctly recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 311, who while in possession sold the same to Defendant No. 6 by kabala dated 27th Aswin 1374 B.S. Ext. C, who has been possessing mutating the name in the Khatian and payment of rent vide Ext. E series there was no illegality in the impugned judgment dismissing the suit setting aside the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below. 

7. The plaintiffs based their claim on the basis of patta Ext. 1 dated 7th Aswin 1281 B.S. in favour of Tajumuddin Matbar who died before cadertral survey leaving son Panjat Ali and daughter Pearjan. Panjat All was minor and was under de-facto guardianship of Nizamuddin, father-in-law of Pearjan, sister of Panjat Ali who used to look after and manage the proper-ty left by Tajumuddin Matbar and fraudulently got it recorded 1/3rd share in his name and 1/3rd share in the name of his brother Ahmed All and 1/3rd share in the name of Panjat Ali instead of entire patta land of 5.74 decimals in the name of Panjat All and Pearjan in 2/3rd and 1/3rd share respectively and Panjat All died after C.S. operation leaving his sister Pearjan in his sole heir. Pearjan who died leaving behind one son Hakimuddin who while in possession was murdered in 1946 during the R.S. operation leaving behind minor Nurul Huq Plaintiff No. 1 and Shamsul Huq Plaintiff No. 2 and daughter Noor Meher and widow Rupjan. Noor Meher and Rupjan gifted their share in favour of the plaintiffs whereby plaintiffs became the owners of the entire land of C.S. Khatian No. 191. As such the R.S. Khatian Nos. 690 and 691 were also wrongly recorded the share of the plaintiffs pursuant to wrong C.S. Khatian and subsequently S.A. Khatian Nos. 836 and 311 were also recorded following wrong R.S. Khatian in spite of the recorders other than the plaintiffs having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The defendant, however, concocted certain documents such as alleged Solenama Ext. A. Patta Ext. B and sale deed Ext. C on the basis of alleged certificate case in respect of S.A. Khatian No. 836. 

8. The Defendant No. 6 claiming 1.24 decimals of S.A. Khatian No. 311 asserted that R.S. recorded tenant Rahimjan made a kol raiyati patta to Kaiser Ahmed, the recorded tenant of S.A. Khatian No. 311 who sold the same in favour of Defendant No. 6-respondent. 

9. The defendant alleged riyati patta by heirs of Amjad Ali, the successor-in-interest of Nazimuddin alleging pattan of 1.24 decimals dated 23.4.1945 corresponding to 1360 B.S. at a jama of Tk. 16/- in favour of Rahimjan, who while in possession settled 1.40 acres to Kaiser Ahmed by patta of dated 10th Baishak 1352 B.S. in whose name S.A. Khatian No. 311 was recorded who in his turn while in possession sold 1.24 decimal by kabala dated 27th Aswin 1374 B.S. Ext. C in favour of Defendant No. 6 who has been possessing. 

10. From the above, it appears Rahimjan obtained pattan from the heirs of Amjad Ali but no patta or any rent receipt showing the settlement has been produced in the suit. D.W. 1 has simply stated that the heirs of Amjad Ali patta settled to Rahimjan in 1360 B.S. by Dhakhila for 1.24 acres at a jama of Tk. 16/- but no patta or rent receipt has been produced. D.W. 1 has further deposed that he did not see any dhakhila granted to Rahimjan by the heirs of Amjad Ali. Defendant No. 6, however, asserted that 
the tenancy so created was confirmed by rent suit of the same year of the patta and relied on Solenama Ext. A to show that there was a solenama between Janor Ali and others and Rahimjan but from the certified copy of solenama it does not appear that the heirs of Amzad Ali in fact filed the Rent Suit and entered into a compromise with Rahimjan. Moreover, from the compromise petition, the name of husband of Pearjan has been stated as Ahmed Ali instead of Amzad Ali. These materials do not go to show that Rahimjan ever took any settlement from the heirs Amzad All and others. 

11. Defendant No. 1 deposed that he did not see the solenama in the rent suit filed by the said Amjad Ali. In view of the failure of the defendant to produce the patta or the rent receipt or there being no cogent evidence in support of the solena-ma, the proceeding in alleged rent suit appeared to be collusive one in order to create evidence of settlement in favour of Rahimjan. Thus the defendant has failed to prove the settlement. The defendant has filed Ext. C, the patta in favour of Kaiser Ahmed from Rahimjan for 1.40 acres of suit land but the same is a certified copy and D.W. 1 deposed that he was not pre-sent when Rahimjan gave patta to Kaiser Ahmed and he did not say who wrote the patta and how Rahimjan executed the patta and he could not also say if Kaiser Ahmed ever paid rant to Rahimjan or Rahimjan ever held such land mentioned in the patta. 

12. As regards possession D.W. 1 simply said that he heard that Rahimjan possessed the suit land and thereafter his son possessed. He could not say who possessed the suit land before him. The defendant also admitted the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The plaintiff has filed the suit for declaration of their title on assertion that the suit is in their possession and the recording in C.S., R.S. and S.A. are wrong. Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act provides that a suit for mere declaration of any legal character or any right to property is maintainable and in view of the evidence of possession in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff need not ask for any further relief and the object of the proviso is only to avoid multiplicity of the suit where further relief can be sought for at the time of the institution of the suit. Considering the facts and circumstances of the present suit we hold that the present suit for mere declaration is maintainable. 

13. The suit was for declaration of title of the plaintiff on assertion of possession and that C.S., R.S. and S.A. Khatians are wrong. Defendant has not disputed the quantum of land in patta Ext. 1 or the suit land as claimed by the plaintiff on the basis of the patta or that land of S.A. Khatian No. 311 did not form part of the land of patta Ext. 1 and as such there was no dispute that the suit land was not identical to the land patta Ext. 1 and accordingly no question of relayment in order to ascertain identity of the land was necessary. Thus the High Court Division erred in law in holding that in order to ascertain the suit land claimed by the plaintiff relayment is required and as that was not done by the plaintiff they failed to prove their claim as per pleading. 

14. The plaintiff as well filed Exts. 2 and 3 as to payment of rent on the basis of patta dated 7th Aswin 1381 B.S. and the defendant No. 6 as well filed rent receipt Ext. E series to support their payment of rent in respect of the suit land of S.A. Khatian No. 311. In the case of Lal Meah being dead his heirs Momena Khaton and ors. Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Meah and ors. 28 DLR (AD) 61 it has been held that record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title of land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title. By itself, it is not an evidence of title. The presumption of correctness as available to the C.S. record of right in the name of Nazimuddin's  1/3rd share on the strength of Section 1038(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act has been rebutted as the defendants could not show any basis of record in view of patta Ext. 1 in favour of Tajumuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs. Consequently there are also no basis of recording in R.S. and S.A. in the arnes of the recordees other than the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 6 also could not pro-duce any patta or rent receipt in support of the lease in favour of Rahimjan and as such the rent receipts Ext. D series could not confer any title on the defendant No. 6. The plaintiff led evidence of possession and the same has also been supported by D.Ws. Thus the presumption attached to C.S. has been rebutted and as such sub-sequent recording in R.S. and S.A. are of no legal consequence. The khatian being at best evidence of present possession could not be a document of title so as to confer right, title, and interest of the suit land. The defendant having failed to prove any basis of their title by any cogent material, the rent receipt Ext. E series are of no avail to them. When evidence was led in rebuttal of the presumption of correctness of entry in the record of right and the appellate Court below comes to a finding rebutting the presumption, the said finding being finding of fact, arrived at by the final Court of fact on consideration of the evidence on record, is not liable to be interfered with in revision as there was no error of law resulting in the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The Court of appeal below has considered that no question of any partition in the suit is necessary, as the plaintiff has claimed the entire suit land and mores°, the suit was for declaration of title. 

15. The Court of appeal below also considered the alleged auction sale and held that such alleged auction purchaser D.W.9 admitted that he could not obtain the same certificate and delivery of possession. Thus the sale was not acted upon and the sale did not affect the plaintiffs title arid possession and as such the plaintiffs suit as framed is maintainable. 

16. In the suit the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 7-25, 26 have filed a solenama dated 15.4.1374 and the Court of appeal below has colics.25.red the same and found the terms of the solenan: legal and as there was nothing unfair or in the solenama, accepted the same. 

17. In view of the above, we hold that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the basis of their patta dated 17 Aswin 1281 B.S. but the C.S., R.S. and S.A. Khatian have wrongly recorded other recordees therein other than the plaintiffs. 

18. Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division are not sustainable in law and the same are set aside restoring the judgment and decree dated 18.4.1985 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge decreeing the suit. 

19. In the result, this appeal is allowed with costs. 

End.
